item.title: Up to 10 per cent rise in local homes
item.description: The price of homes in the Shannonside region has increased by up to 10 per cent this year, according to a local auctioneer. That's higher than the national average. CSO data shows they increased by 7.3 per cent around the country in the year to October. Advertisement Joe Brady, from REA Brady in Carrick, says they've increased sharply throughout the region this year: Prices are also increasing for rental homes. item.title: Tributes paid to the late Jim Nolan
item.description: Tributes have been paid to a former trade unionist and Labour election candidate following his death this week. Jim Nolan was a native of Keadue in County Roscommon who ran unsuccessfully in the 1992 General Election. Mr Nolan was a well-known community activist who represented the party in Longford-Roscommon constituency. item.title: Over €1.5 million awarded to county Roscommon projects
item.description: Three county Roscommon projects have been awarded funding under Fáilte Ireland's Regenerative Tourism and Placemaking Scheme. The fund aims to address employment, economic, social and environmental impacts that come with the shift away from carbon-intense activities. The Irish Heritage Trust is to receive 1.2 million euro for the development of outdoor areas and trails to create an engaging and family friendly visitor experience at Strokestown Park. item.title: Calls for minimum wage to be extended
item.description: A local Senator has called for the national minimum wage to be extended to young workers, apprentices and interns. Sligo-Leitrim Senator Nessa Cosgrove told the Seanad apprentices, interns and young people continue to face unfairly low wages, with some first-year apprentices earning far below the minimum wage. item.title: Lack of local domestic violence refuges highlighted
item.description: The Shannonside region has been highlighted for a lack in refuges for victims of domestic violence. Sinn Féin Senator Pauline Tully told the Seanad that the local area needs more funding to be allocated towards better refuge for affected women and children. Longford, Leitrim and Roscommon were mentioned in a collection of counties without a refuge space for domestic violence victims. item.title: Popular Longford market announces schedule change
item.description: The popular Longford Indoor Market and Car Boot has announced a major change to its weekly schedule. It will move from its long-standing Saturday slot to every Sunday from January 11th, 2026. Organisers confirmed the new arrangement on social media this week with it set to remain at Mastertech Business Park on the Athlone Road. item.title: Flu continues to impact the local region
item.description: The flu will continue to impact people in Shannonside region. That's despite cases falling locally and latest forecasts indicating that between 800 to 1,100 people are expected to be hospitalised. While earlier this week, it emerged that flu rates in county Leitrim are higher than the national average. item.title: Allianz to remain as GAA sponsor
item.description: The GAA has decided to continue their sponsorship relationship with Allianz. Allianz have been long term sponsors of the national football and hurling leagues. A number of county boards including Roscommon and Leitrim moved proposals to central council to remove Allianz as a sponsor. However, the GAA’s Coiste Bainistíochta has decided to retain the Allianz sponsorship.
